VladTV sits down with political operatives Jack Burkman and Jacob Wohl for a wide-ranging interview covering their legal controversies, business disputes, and the ongoing fallout involving Boosie. Vlad presses the pair on whether they feel Boosie’s actions amount to “snitching,” while Burkman and Wohl discuss arbitration, alleged phone harassment, and why they say the case should be dismissed.

Wohl also addresses his past as the so-called “youngest hedge fund manager,” the National Futures Association lifetime ban, Arizona Corporate Commission action, and his California felony tied to selling an unregistered security. The conversation expands into Donald Trump, Joe Biden, IRS audits, alleged de-banking, FISA warrants, Google notices, the FBI, and the Michigan robocall case involving Attorney General Dana Nessel.

Vlad closes with a business lesson: get every deal in writing, especially when major money and public figures are involved.

recentItems.title: Vlad Responds to Yung Bleu Leaking Texts, Demanding $50K for Interview, Boxing Challenge
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
In this VladTV response, DJ Vlad revisits his long-running fallout with Yung Bleu, from their 2018 introduction through Bleu’s Drake-assisted breakout and reported $5M Empire deal. Vlad says Bleu privately disputed Boosie Badazz’s royalty demands, claimed he offered Boosie $2M, and later asked Vlad to contribute $50K toward Boosie’s legal fees after a gun-charge arrest—an allegation Boosie denied on camera. He also addresses Bleu posting their text messages, insisting he reached out to discuss past issues, not book a paid interview. The response touches on Bleu’s “Reading the Room,” recent projects including Bleu Vandross 4 and World at War, Spotify/YouTube numbers, tour dates in Joliet and Pasadena, and loyalty debates around Drake vs. Kendrick Lamar. Vlad also references Rod Wave, Charleston White, N.O.R.E., Aries Spears, Angela Yee, and his own split with Boosie over interview money.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Denvonta “Dirt Rocc” Lee looks back on hearing the news of 2Pac’s death while locked up and explains how the aftermath was felt inside jail. Speaking with DJ Vlad, Dirt Rocc recalls watching the coverage in the day room with other Crips, then later seeing footage of Orlando Anderson being jumped and understanding why tensions were escalating. He describes how the conflict between South Side Crips and MOB Piru intensified in Compton after Tupac Shakur died, with shootings and retaliation reported on both sides. While he was behind bars, Dirt Rocc says he heard updates from the streets and remained prepared for confrontations with rivals inside, leading to two fights in jail tied to the ongoing feud. The conversation also references Mob James, Neck Bone, and the wider impact of the 1996 2Pac tragedy on Los Angeles gang politics.

--------
Former Navy SEAL Robert O’Neill and former Army Ranger sniper Nicholas Irving join Vlad to compare the world’s elite special operations units, including SEAL Team Six, Delta Force, the 22 SAS, SBS, Canada’s Joint Task Force 2, Rangers, and the 160th SOAR “Night Stalkers.” O’Neill explains why night vision, communications, air superiority, and insertion platforms can decide a mission, recalling a vehicle interdiction operation in Baghdad involving multiple Tier One forces. Irving agrees that at the highest level, units like Delta and SEAL Team Six are nearly impossible to separate in capability, while noting the U.S. advantage in funding. The conversation also breaks down SEAL Team Six selection, Delta Force recruiting, the rumored “Long Walk” through the Appalachian Mountains, and the role of Rangers and Air Force support in high-risk operations.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/s5i3shO8ImI
--------
In this VladTV conversation, TS Madison breaks down how her viral basement rant became part of Beyoncé’s *Renaissance* standout “Cozy.” Madison reveals that the sample request first came through a pseudonym before she later saw Parkwood in the paperwork while vacationing in Costa Rica, prompting her attorneys to handle the clearance. She explains the emotional origin of the clip, connecting it to the outrage surrounding George Floyd’s murder in Minneapolis and the attack on trans woman Ayana Dior in Minnesota, and why she felt compelled to speak on Black trans visibility and injustice.

Madison also recalls the moment she realized Beyoncé had used her voice, meeting Bey in person, and sharing an emotional laugh over the now-iconic line. Plus, she confirms receiving a Grammy certificate for her contribution to “Cozy” and reflects on Beyoncé’s presence, family, and impact.

--------
In this VladTV conversation, T.K. Kirkland reacts as Vlad discusses claims he heard about Keefe D, Compton, and the alleged personal motivation behind his interviews and book. Vlad says a source connected Keefe D’s media appearances—including a paid interview—to money he wanted to spend on a longtime girlfriend from the “D-boy era,” even suggesting he talked too much publicly to impress or keep her around. Kirkland weighs in on the dangers of chasing celebrity, viral fame, and social media attention when there’s no real foundation behind it.

The discussion expands into how going viral rarely creates lasting success, with references to Bhad Bhabie, OnlyFans, Jay-Z, The Black Album, and Jay-Z’s former A&R Hip Hop. Kirkland also reflects on longevity in stand-up comedy, staying consistent, having a real story, and why talent plus substance matters more than quick fame.
